finding.claim: The DELETE handler calls authorized(), which returns a boolean, and ignores the result. The authorization check is never enforced, so any authenticated user can delete any project. Unlike authorize(), authorized() does not throw.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sends DELETE /projects/:id with an id they do not own. They need no admin rights.

trace.note: Route handler for DELETE /projects/:id; id comes from req.params.
Project is fetched by the attacker-supplied id with no ownership filter.
authorized(req.user, project) returns true or false. The return value is discarded and nothing throws.
Responds 204, so the deletion succeeds for the attacker.

finding.guards_checked: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and is not used in a conditional. authorize() at api.js:4-10, which throws on failure, is only used in the PUT route. The file has no middleware that enforces ownership. Authentication middleware that sets req.user lives outside this file and is not present. It would not enforce per-resource ownership in any case.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and its result is discarded at api.js:18. authorize() at api.js:4-10 throws but is only called in the PUT route at api.js:25. There is no other middleware in the file.
verdict.reason: At api.js:18 the boolean returned by authorized() is discarded, so api.js:19 deletes the project and api.js:20 returns 204 for any authenticated user, whether or not they own it.
